Honda Has a Taste of the e-MTB World with the RN0 Motor-Assisted Bicycle
97 photos
Photo: Honda
If I am to be generous, I could say there are around 20 major motorcycle makers in the world right now. Of that, only a fraction are also involved in making bicycles, be them powered in one way or another, or simply pedal-operated. Technically speaking, Honda isn't one of them. Or wasn't, as this week, during the EICMA show in Milan, it presented something special.
Enter the RN0, an electric mountain bike (e-MTB) that marks the Japanese company's formal entry into a realm it tried before, but never decided to commit to, and its first motor-assisted bicycle. Built together with Germany-based specialist ROTWILD , it is supposed to open up a whole new chapter in the company's history.
The bike is built around a carbon monocoque frame that was inspired by the world of motorcycles, and uses the bike maker's gullwing swingarm and linkage system. It is propped on DT Swiss wheels sized 29 inches at the front and 27.5 inches at the rear, with Schwalbe rubber making the connection to the ground.
A suspension system supplied by Fox, comprised of a fork at the front and a shock at the rear, is what aids riders when moving over difficult terrain, while braking power comes courtesy of hardware supplied by Shimano.
This being an electric bicycle and all, it does need to have the proper powertrain. For the task at hand, Honda went for a Shimano drive unit and a removable 720Wh battery. The motor fitted on the RN0 is potent enough to generate 750W of power and 100 Nm of torque.
The 12-speed Shimano Deore XT Di2 drivetrain that was included in the design is made in such a way as to optimize gear selection and traction no matter if the bike is climbing or descending.
Honda integrated a 2.2-inch display into the top tube, and even provides a USB-C charging port for riders to be able to charge and connect devices. The Shimano Connect mobile app works with the new bicycle.
With all these fittings on, the bike is as light as you'd expect from a player in this segment, tipping the scales at 52 pounds (23.5 kg)
Honda didn't specifically say when the RN0 will hit the market, but I expect that to happen early next year. It's too early to tell how much the Japanese will charge for it, but to give you a taste of what to expect, I will tell you that the company refers to this vehicle using the word premium.
There will be three sizes on the table, S, M, and L, each of them individually engineered with size-specific dimensions. Only one color was announced for now for the frame, something called Pearl Moon Ash Gray, which matches the Ergon SM10 saddle.
